Olga — draft answers and rationale below. I kept the language concise for inclusion in their packet; we can expand in the appendix if they want implementation details.

1) Storage location by default- Hosted API request/response payloads and generated artifacts are persisted in the tenancy's primary region. For self‑serve accounts we default to the region closest to the sign‑up location (US-west for NA customers). For customers requiring EU-only storage we offer EU tenancy pinning as part of the hosted-enterprise contract (data residency addendum).

2) Default retention windows (hosted API)
- Request/response logs (application payloads): default 30 days; configurable to 90/365 via contract for enterprise plans.
- Streaming/KV caches: ephemeral, retained only in memory and short local caches (<1 hour) unless explicitly persisted by customer choice.
- Embeddings & derived vectors: default 14 days; can be configured to 7 days (strict ephemeral) or retained longer if customer elects persistent vector storage under SLA.
- Model artifacts (snapshots, fine‑tuned artifacts): retained until explicitly deleted; default snapshot retention 30 days for rolling backups.

3) Erasure / tenant termination timelines
- On an account termination/erasure request we stop serving traffic immediately and mark tenant datasets for purge. Primary store purge: typical completion within 30 days.
- Backups / long‑term snapshots: fully scrubbed within 90 days (this accounts for cross‑region replication and backup windows). We provide a certificate of deletion on request after completion.

4) Backups & cross‑region replication
- Backups are scheduled per tenancy and may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA. For customers who require EU‑only custody we ensure backups remain in‑region; cross‑region replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted.
- Maximum backup retention default is 90 days; longer retention available under contract.

5) Key management & auditability
- KMS: Redwood uses cloud KMS by default for encryption at rest; enterprise customers can provide customer‑managed keys (CMKs) or integrate with HSMs in private deployments.
- Audit logs: deletion and erasure events are logged and retained for 365 days by default in our audit trail (accessible to customers via the console for enterprise accounts). Logs include the user, timestamp, object id, and operation status.

Notes on evidence: I attached the small residency matrix and architecture diagram if they want an appendix entry. Suggest we offer Crestline the EU tenancy addendum and a 30‑day primary purge / 90‑day backup scrub cadence in writing; that should be acceptable for their board.

If that reads OK, Olga, happy for you to send to Emma.

— Karthik
Director, Infrastructure Product
Redwood Inference

Hi Emma — thanks for the note and the SQ. Please find our short answers below; I’ve attached a one‑page summary and the draft responses for inclusion in your packet. If your board needs tighter timelines, we can add the EU tenancy addendum and a CMK option to the order form.

Summary answers (for packet)
• Storage location: Hosted API data is persisted in the tenancy’s primary region. Self‑serve accounts default to the nearest regional cluster (US by default); EU‑only tenancy pinning is available under enterprise contract.
• Default retention: Request/response payloads are retained 30 days by default (configurable to 90/365 for enterprise). Embeddings retained 14 days by default (can be reduced to 7 days). Model snapshots retained until deleted; rolling snapshot retention default 30 days.
• Erasure timelines: Primary data purge within 30 days after a verified erasure request or tenant termination. Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days; we provide a deletion attestation on completion.
• Backups & replication: Backups may replicate to a secondary region for DR depending on SLA; for EU‑only contracts cross‑region replication is disabled. Max default backup retention 90 days (extendable by agreement).
• KMS & audit: Encryption at rest via cloud KMS by default; enterprise customers may use customer‑managed keys or HSMs. Deletion/erasure events are logged in the audit trail (365‑day retention) and can be surfaced in the console or delivered as an export for enterprise customers.
